We are the result of our actions and in long term good actions are executed by heart.

The hunger to excel has always pushed me towards my goal. During College, I made sure to have a diverse exposure which should give me an edge over my peers by making optimum use of my resources. As a result, I received the highest package CTC in my college. I took a leap to service industry instead of going to a core sector considering my strengths of leadership and interpersonal skills. My brief stint at TAGIC helped me to gain analytical and logical skills at the same time helping me to work efficiently in a corporate environment.

I always desired of going the Startup way given my background of being from a business family. I left my well-paying job and took up a risky uncertain decision of being part of a startup. The ride in Startup was not as smooth as being in a job and I had to go through many failures and setbacks. This challenge made me realize my potential and helped me come out of my comfort zone.

My future goals are in sync with my role as a CEO and the decision of being in a business school is to upgrade my skills of big data analysis, market changes which will help me to take critical decisions. Another factor when considering an MBA degree as a startup owner is the network I will be building in XLRI and have a much higher chance of success with our startup.

Through this program I aspire to hone the ability to truly build global business competence, through both the content and context of the experience. The Global MBA program is the first MBA program that takes place in 3 of the most important economic regions of the world, and also has an extended curriculum specifically tailored to explore global markets, regulations, and business institutions. The trans-cultural exposure teaches to look at things from multiple angles. 
To lead in a global economy, one must be able to not only identify and interpret, but also reconcile the various drivers shaping today`s complex business environment. To drive this level of global business awareness and analysis, I think that a Global MBA Degree, which brings together eager aspirants of varying nationalities , with all their diverse backgrounds and experiences, for a rigorous business management education that integrates learning experiences across economies. I hope to learn about the social, economic, political, historical, and cultural issues that influence business around the world so that I can, in turn, effectively lead and manage a global operation.
Three projects in leading companies (one in each country) to will develop an appreciation of corporate functioning there in addition to giving an added advantage over the one internship which normal MBA requires. While in-region, I will learn about different cultures, markets, and institutions, while experiencing them at the same time. Cross-cultural communication is part of the subject matter and the situation itself, which will better prepare me for international leadership responsibilities.

Having worked in the field of Business Intelligence and Analytics for over 20 years, I would like to put to use the knowledge and experience I gained, to do my PhD in Information Systems. This will help me contribute towards advancements in emerging technologies, i.e., Analytics using Big Data and Cloud Computing. For the past few decades large organizations are struggling to keep pace with Big Data characterized by high volume, high velocity and high variety of data. This requirement has also driven hardware platforms to the bleeding edge pushing for a Cloud-based Elastic Storage systems. 

There are many on-going open source projects like Apache Hadoop focused on accelerating the pace of development in Big Data. But, there are as many problems to handle as the same time. Not only that we have to find answer for effective storage of Big Data, the extraction and manipulation of such complex data is equally challenging. I would like to contribute towards the rapid development of Big Data on Cloud platform through the XLRI Executive FPM course offering.

 	Right from the beginning of my corporate career I had a strong inclination for research and development. My interest in the subject has grown with each passing year and now it has reached to a point where even PhD may not quench my thirst for knowledge and innovation. I have come to terms with the fact that there is an enormous proportion of subject to be assimilated. I want to take up a research oriented course to give a direction to my thought process and turn it as practical and commercially viable as possible.

R24014.sop:
With close to 25 years of experience in the Industry across various sectors and in the HR leadership role during last 10 years, my next career objective is to be become a HR / Management Consultant in the next 5 years. Not limiting my industry experience, enhancing knowledge through a research based approach is very critical for me to achieve my career objective. In view of this I aim to complete Executive PhD program. The proposed topic is of great interest to me and to start gaining more insights, I have done literature review and conducted an internal study through focused group discussions. The proposed research topic is `Manager???s role in understanding and managing Gen Z Employee Expectations for better Retention in Healthcare Sector in India`. 
Research Objective: To discover key attributes that would help the Reporting/Immediate Manager???s for them to have better understanding of Gen Z employee expectations and manage the same for better retention specific to Healthcare Sector in India. While there are publications and research papers on what motivates Gen Z employees in an organisation, there are very few or almost NIL research-based insights/studies on Key Attributes a Manager should develop that would help them understand and manage Gen Z employee expectations for better retention. On further search / investigation, there are NIL research publications / research work specific to Gen Z employees working in the India Healthcare Sector. The India healthcare sector comes with its own people related challenges such as burnout, limitation in adoption of new technology, skill enhancement, availability of talent etc. Hence, retention of employees and Gen Z employees in particular is very critical. Towards this purpose, we seek an answer to the following research question: What are the key attributes a manager should develop to understand and manage Gen Z employee expectations for better retention specific to healthcare in India?

In my current role as Lead- Communication & Employer Branding, which essentially falls at the cusp of HR and Marketing, I have often felt that I could add much more value to the role and my organisation, had I been able to strategically improvise Employee experience through interventions across HR processes and employee life cycle as a whole. Now some of these changes could be quick-fixes, while some essentially hits the organisation culture & the existing frameworks.

Being in an early stage talent organisation, its still more open to conceive and implement such changes, but as the organisation grows & matures or even as I personally move to much bigger and older organisations, I see it becoming more difficult.

I feel both people and business(read marketing) side have equal importance in my role. But essentially being a marketer by qualification, I do tend to weigh heavier on the marketing side of it. As I grow even in my current role, I would like to balance that out with people outlook.

Also, keeping the current situation in perspective, the amount of change that???s already hit the organisations has been quite detrimental. Its not just the game to be better now as employers, its become a game of survival. What we are facing today will essentially change the way we have ever functioned. And before more such changes hit us like that, we need to better prepared and agile in our people strategy.

I feel this program will help to open up the view with which I perceive people strategy for organisations at various stages of their evolution. I also expect this program to equip me with the skills to help me and my organisation navigate through these situations better.
This will also pave a growth path for me in my career to move ahead in more strategic roles and be able to create more value as an HR professional, to the business and to my people.
